AboutMe.subtitle: MORE ABOUT ME
AboutMe.title: I'm Çağlar, a
AboutMe.description1: I’m a Software Engineer with 4 years of professional experience across AI infrastructure, backend systems, and full-stack product development. I enjoy taking ownership of problems from the first investigation through implementation, deployment, and ongoing reliability. At Frist, I worked on the infrastructure and tools behind AI agent training and evaluation. My work spanned model-serving performance, training workflows, monitoring, access-controlled APIs, and research dashboards. This involved tracing bottlenecks across application and infrastructure layers, making experiments easier to reproduce, and keeping research data reliable through production changes.
AboutMe.description2: Earlier in my career, I built e-commerce and business automation software, co-founded a computer-vision startup, and developed an AI-powered education platform serving more than 3,000 active users. Working closely with customers and researchers taught me to connect engineering decisions to the people using the product. I’m particularly interested in backend engineering, AI infrastructure, and product roles where I can contribute across system boundaries and own features end to end. Based in Türkiye, I’m open to fully remote opportunities with international teams.
AboutMe.quote: I believe in waking up each day eager to make a difference!

Timeline.mainDescription: My professional journey over the years
Timeline.job1Description: AI company with $10M in funding, building training systems for agents that use computers.
Timeline.job2Title: Business Analyst & Software Engineer @ Çetintaş Bilgi Teknolojileri / Didoda A.Ş.
Timeline.job2Description: Technology company providing ERP solutions and regulatory software integrations.
Timeline.job3Description: Software agency developing enterprise e-commerce and warehouse management systems.
Timeline.job4Description: IoT and computer-vision startup developing enterprise automation systems.
job1Bullets: I engineered distributed training infrastructure with Ray, NCCL and HSDP across two GPU environments (48 NVIDIA H100s and 64 NVIDIA H200s), with W&B, Kubernetes and Ray orchestration that recovers from restarts and terminates stalled jobs to protect GPU capacity.
I cut average model response time by over 50% in a single-node test by optimizing screenshot preprocessing, and cut a full scan of saved training runs from 125 seconds to 5.1 seconds.
I migrated production to PostgreSQL and S3, preserving 708 evaluation results and 793 artifacts, and built authorized, auditable REST APIs for inspecting and stopping training jobs.

I also built a research dashboard for comparing results across 14 AI benchmarks, an evaluation harness that measured 85% accuracy across 410 page predictions, and a detection system that uses LLM judges and video-based checks to find where AI-generated website clones behave differently from the real sites.
job2Bullets: I led business analysis for an Odoo ERP project at a currency-exchange holding with 6 hospitality venues (3 restaurants, 2 cafés and a nightclub), from gap analysis through go-live.
As the client's main point of contact, I turned business requirements into specifications for their in-house developers and managed scope and change requests.

I built the on-premise servers for the deployment, advised the client's developers and team leads on integration design, wrote Python features and fixes for Odoo when the project needed extra capacity, and ran acceptance testing with venue staff.
job3Bullets: I improved e-commerce page load speed by 60% through a Vue 3 and TypeScript rebuild, and fixed concurrency and memory issues as part of a 15-member team.
job4Bullets: As co-founder of a 12-person team, I built backend systems and workflow automation for Mercedes-Benz authorized service centers and handled client meetings and product planning.
I also engineered a computer-vision system that detects 12 solar-panel defect classes for quality inspection.

coach.name: Coach Connect
coach.description: A study-coaching marketplace with 3,000 active users that connects coaches with students preparing for Türkiye's university entrance exam (YKS).
coach.b1: Go REST API on PostgreSQL with role-based access for students, coaches and admins, background jobs and push notifications.
coach.b2: Split payments with iyzico that hold funds until the coaching period ends, then pay the coach minus the platform's commission.
coach.b3: Coach rankings based on students' practice-exam results, and risk scoring that shows coaches which students are falling behind.
coach.b4: Student app in React and TypeScript: find a coach, buy a package, track weekly progress and join video calls.
coach.b5: In progress: a permission-scoped RAG assistant that lets coaches search each student's notes and call summaries, using hybrid search (pgvector + Postgres full-text) and SQL tools for exam data.

forge.name: forge
forge.description: An autonomous development-workflow MCP server in Go for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex CLI.
forge.b1: Takes a ticket or plain-English goal to a merged pull request. A deterministic engine owns the workflow and gives the LLM one step at a time, so the agent cannot drift from the process.
forge.b2: Runs in parallel in separate git worktrees, with adversarial review agents that caught real defects before merge.
